I will keep cotton as my main crop because that is the crop system I know best, it fits my land and experience, and with 9.5 mu plus well irrigation I can manage it steadily without spreading my labor too thin. I will put most of the land into cotton for reliable income, keep a smaller area of cauliflower for cash flow, and plant a modest area of stevia as a higher-value side crop without taking too much risk. I have farmed for 35 years, so I do not want an aggressive plan with very high fertilizer or spray use. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps stand establishment and yield, plough the cotton and stevia land to prepare a clean seedbed, and use rotary tillage for cauliflower because it is enough for that crop and saves labor. Since I have well irrigation, I will irrigate enough to protect emergence and key growth stages, but I will not overwater. I will keep fertilizer moderate and practical, with cotton getting the most balanced nutrient investment, cauliflower getting higher nitrogen for head growth, and stevia getting enough fertility for leaf production. I will also keep pesticide sprays to a moderate level and only plan for the number I think I will realistically need in a normal year.
